correctness.rationale: A common plank normal reduces the covered set inside the Euclidean ball to a measurable subset of one coordinate interval. Exact ball slicing gives an integral against an even strictly decreasing density. Symmetric decreasing rearrangement proves the optimum and equality conditions, while the beta substitution gives the closed form. In the equal-measure stability regime, the least costly removal and most profitable exterior addition are the adjacent boundary layers, yielding the sharp deficit. The bundled checker independently reproduces all formulas and equality constructions.
risks: The finite numerical replay is not used to prove any quantified statement.

value.rationale: The aligned family is not an arbitrary restriction: it is exactly the geometric configuration the source conjectures to maximize covered volume. The theorem establishes that target on the complete parallel subclass in every dimension, gives the exact benchmark value required by the wider problem, classifies all equality families, and supplies an optimal quantitative placement deficit. This isolates the cross-direction interaction as the only remaining obstruction within the source problem.
risks: The full arbitrary-direction conjecture remains open in dimensions not covered by known special results.
